Everything you need to ship from India to Argentina or import from Argentina to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Argentina at a glance
India–Mercosur Preferential Trade Agreement (in force since 2009). Expansion talks launched in September 2026.

India exports vehicles and two-wheelers, agrochemicals, organic chemicals, pharmaceuticals, yarn and engineering goods. India is one of the largest buyers of Argentine soybean oil, and also imports pulses (lentils, chickpeas), sunflower oil, hides and lithium.
Routes and transit times to Argentina

35–45 days to Buenos Aires, usually with transhipment (often via Santos or Montevideo). Direct East Coast South America services from Nhava Sheva/Mundra (around the Cape of Good Hope), or transhipment via Colombo, Singapore or Jebel Ali.
4–7 days via Europe, the Gulf or São Paulo.
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Argentina: what your buyer needs
The importer needs a CUIT and must be registered as an importer with customs (ARCA, formerly AFIP).
The SEDI advance-information system was repealed in 2025 and import controls have been simplified significantly since 2024.
A licensed customs broker (despachante de aduana) files the import.
Foreign-exchange access for paying suppliers has been eased since 2024–25, but confirm your buyer's bank can pay on your terms before shipping.
Mercosur TEC (mostly 0–35%, with many cuts since 2024), plus 21% VAT (IVA) and VAT and income-tax perceptions, and the statistics fee. Rates have changed often recently: check before quoting.
ANMAT: medicines, food, cosmetics, medical devices
SENASA: plant and animal health (agri imports, wood packaging)
Technical safety certification for electrical goods (often relaxed recently, so check)
Mercosur PTA certificate of origin for preference

From Argentina to India, and tips from the field
Soybean oil (crude degummed) and pulses are the big flows. Pulses into India need plant quarantine permits and are subject to India's pulse import policy (check DGFT notifications).
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Policy changes are frequent: always check the latest resolution before quoting duty.
River draught limits at Rosario affect bulk vessel sizes.
